newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy urges higher Med offshore hydrocarbon output.
newsitem.headline: Italy urges higher Med offshore hydrocarbon output.

text.p: Franco Bernabe, chief executive of Italian state-controlled energy giant Ente Nazionale Idrocarburi Spa (ENI), on Wednesday stressed the need to boost Mediterranean offshore hydrocarbons output.
Addressing the opening of the third Offshore Mediterranean Conference, he said that eventually Mediterranean offshore production should aim to meet a similar output to that of Saudi Arabia.
"Global oil and gas demand is increasing by 3.5 million barrels per day equivalent. We need to find potential reserves to cover seven million bpd, half in production and half reserves," he said.
"The Mediterranean offshore industry should aim to meet output similar to that of Saudi Arabia," Bernabe said without giving any figures.
He noted that the offshore industry, one of Italy's main industries, was growing and expanding to the eastern Mediterranean basin with countries like Egypt and Libya.

Italian Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani told the international energy meeting that Italy had a leading role in the global offshore industry, with offshore output providing one third of Italy's crude oil demand.
"There are 110 platforms in and around Italy and we have 60 international companies operating in Italy," Bersani said.
"The sector has a national role and there is now an extraordinary opportunity to develop accords and boost collaboration with other Mediterranean nations," Bersani said.
